articles.title: First Direct Image of a Cosmic Web Filament Confirms How Galaxies Are Fed
articles.summary: After hundreds of hours of telescope time, astronomers captured the sharpest image ever of a cosmic filament—a 3-million-light-year-long strand of gas connecting two ancient galaxies. This direct view confirms that these dark-matter highways channel fuel for star formation across the universe.

articles.title: Watch NASA's Next-Gen Mars Rotor Break the Sound Barrier in Simulated Tests
articles.summary: In a series of 137 tests, NASA engineers spun experimental Mars helicopter rotors to supersonic speeds—up to Mach 1.08—inside a chamber that mimics the Red Planet's thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere. The data could boost future rotorcraft lift by 30%, enabling heavier payloads and longer flights.

articles.title: Ethiopian Fossil Teeth Upend Linear View of Human Evolution
articles.summary: Thirteen fossil teeth from Ethiopia reveal that two distinct hominin species—early Homo and an unidentified Australopithecus—coexisted 2.6 to 2.8 million years ago. The discovery challenges the idea of a simple evolutionary march and supports a bushy family tree with overlapping lineages.
